speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I see you are experiencing agitation, jaundice (yellowish skin and eyes), and abnormal lab results. To understand the cause of your condition, I need to ask a few questions: What specific symptoms are you feeling besides the jaundice, and have you noticed any changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B with cocaine-induced liver injury (Toxic Hepatitis).

Please confirm if you have experienced any recent flu-like symptoms such as fever, fatigue, or abdominal pain prior to the jaundice. Additionally, I need to see the results of your liver function tests and viral serology to confirm the diagnosis.
